Return only the shortest standalone answer that preserves every unique fact. No heading, label, preamble, recap or explanation of what the reader should infer. Combine related facts into complete sentences; mention each fact once. Attach evidence IDs in parentheses. Prefer specific verbs and short clauses. Remove redundant implications, repeated subjects and conversational framing. Aim for 35–45 words for verbose material; meaning wins if more are essential.

Preserve every result, condition, exclusion, uncertainty, owner and next action. Preserve exact numbers, units, names, field names, paths, commands, errors, frontmatter and code blocks. Do not claim an instruction happened or an untested result passed. Check all source facts silently before answering.

Already concise: copy EXACTLY. Requested JSON: exact keys/types, no surrounding text. Explicitly requested detail: retain ordered steps, reasons and provenance.

Existing memo edits require requested preview and approved revision-checked memo.write. Stop on conflicts; preserve source evidence. Use one normal drafting call.

Write the requested deliverable from the supplied source. Preserve every substantive fact, constraint, uncertainty, provenance and next action. Do not invent information. Return only the deliverable, with no account of your editing process.

Deliverable surface: memo.
Write a concise standalone API migration note.

Source:
This note should explain the change to the pagination response and should preserve the compatibility details rather than merely saying that pagination was improved. Version 2 adds the next_cursor field. Version 1 clients continue to receive their existing items field, and that field is not being removed. A null next_cursor means that the captured result has no further page. Results are captured once for a query. Files created after that capture do not appear in later pages of the same result. A caller that needs current files must start a new query instead of expecting the cursor to refresh the tree. Cursor state expires when the run is retired. These decisions are specified in api-pagination-2, which is the evidence reference for the migration. The next action is to update the client example so that it follows next_cursor until it is null. There is no change to write permissions or file ownership as part of this API change.

message.content:
**API Migration Note: Pagination Response (v2)**

Version 2 adds the `next_cursor` field. Version 1 clients continue to receive the existing `items` field; it is not removed. A null `next_cursor` means no further page. Results are captured once per query; files created after capture do not appear in later pages. Callers needing current files must start a new query. Cursor state expires when the run is retired. No change to write permissions or file ownership. Next action: update the client example to follow `next_cursor` until null. (api-pagination-2)
